newsitem.title: USA: Krystal to be acquired by Port Royal.
newsitem.headline: Krystal to be acquired by Port Royal.

text.p: Krystal Co., a fast-food restaurant chain, said Thursday it has agreed to be acquired by Port Royal Holdings Inc. for $14.50 cash per share, or about $108.8 million.
Krystal stock jumped $7.25, or 116 percent, to $13.50 in afternoon trading on Nasdaq, where it was the biggest percentage gainer.
Port Royal is a closely held corporation formed by Philip Sanford, senior vice president of Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc., the largest bottler of Coca-Cola Co. products.
Sanford, who has advised the bottler of his intention to resign, will become chairman of Krystal when the transaction is completed. Krystal will remain based in Chatanooga, Tenn.
Krystal said its board has unanimously approved the deal and recommended acceptance by shareholders.

Krystal said holders of 53.3 percent of its 7.5 million shares outstanding have agreed to vote in favour of the merger and have granted Port Royal an option to buy their shares at $14.50 a share in cash.
A proxy statement will be mailed by Aug. 8 to shareholders of record as of July 18 and a special meeting of shareholders will be held by Sept. 8 to vote on the transaction, it said.

R.B. Davenport, chairman of Krystal's executive committee and its largest shareholder, said he is pleased with the transaction and considers it to be "in the best interest" of the company's shareholders.

Krystal owns and operates 249 Krystal and drive-through Krystal Kwik burger restaurants in Alabama, Arakansas, Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi, South Carolina and Tennessee. It also franchises 93 restaurants in those states and in North Carolina.
